Welcome to Lee-on-the-Solent Junior School
A message from the Headteacher
Welcome to the website of Lee-on-the-Solent Junior School.​Lee-on-the-Solent Junior School is a happy and caring school community built on our Sails values of: Self-regulation, independence, focus, boundaries, resilience and respect. Our school vision ‘Sailing into the future’ enables children to understand that they are on a learning journey that promotes citizenship and prepares them for their next stage in education. At our school, we promote building positive relationships, respect for others and the importance of actively listening to all members of the school community. We have a rich and exciting curriculum where all learners are given every opportunity to be the best that they can be.​Lucy Faulkner – Headteacher
Get in contact with us
General Enquiries
General Enquiries should be directed to the school office. Our staff will be happy to help.​If you would like paper copies of any of our correspondence or policies please contact the school office where these will be provided free of charge.

Special Educational Needs
At Lee-on-the-Solent Junior School we want every child to achieve their best and become confident individuals who lead fulfilling lives. Our goal is to remove barriers to learning and participation so that each child can reach their fullest potential irrespective of their ability or needs.
We understand that each pupil has individual and unique needs. However, some pupils require more support and scaffolding than others to achieve well. We recognise that pupils learn at different rates and that there are many factors influencing achievement. Our aim is to identify barriers to learning and ensure that we address these both inside and outside of the classroom.
Our Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator is Mrs Holloway. She can be contacted via the school office.

Sport Premium
What is the Sports Premium?
Funding from central Government is allocated to all schools with primary aged children to improve the quality of Sport and PE provision for all their pupils.
We strongly believe in the health, social and emotional benefits of high quality Sport and PE for all our children and believe that the enhanced provision and enriched programme that the Sports Premium funding is helping us to provide will ensure maximum impact on learning both in and beyond the school environment.

Clubs & Activities
At Lee-on-the-Solent Junior School we value the extension of learning to promote fitness, to learn a new skill and, most importantly, to have fun.
This academic year, we will have a wide variety of clubs on offer to pupils, with the activities available changing each term. The range of clubs run each term will depend on availability of staff, expertise and interest, cost and time of year.
To see our full range of clubs, please click here.
The majority of our clubs are run free of charge by dedicated school staff; we are also pleased to be able to accommodate outside providers back on to our school site to run some paid clubs.
Clubs run by our fantastic staff will be on offer at the following times:
A message will be sent out each term, enabling you to sign your child up for the club of their choice. There will be an equal number of clubs made available to each year group across the year. There are some clubs that are by invitation only. In this instance, you will be contacted if your child is selected to take part.

Pupil Premium
The Pupil Premium is an additional grant of money provided to schools by the government aimed at reducing the educational effects of disadvantage.
The Pupil Premium is allocated to children from low-income families who are currently known to be eligible, or have been in the last 6 years, for Free School Meals (FSM) and to children who are in Local Authority care.
Schools in England can receive the Pupil Premium for children adopted from care, or who left care under a Special Guardianship Order on or after 30 December 2005. Schools can also claim the Pupil Premium for children who left care under a Residence Order on or after 14 October 1991.
A smaller amount is allocated to children whose parents are currently serving in the armed forces to address the emotional and social well-being of these pupils.
As a group, children who have been eligible for FSM at any point in time have consistently lower educational attainment than those who have never been eligible for FSM. For children who have entered Local Authority care, the attainment gap is even wider. The Pupil Premium is to help schools raise the attainment of disadvantaged pupils and close the gap with their peers. It is paid to schools in respect of disadvantaged pupils in Reception to Year 11.
It is for schools to decide how the Pupil Premium is spent, since the government’s view is that they are best placed to assess what additional provision should be made for the individual pupils within their responsibility.

Vision & Values
Our vision is to provide memorable, purposeful and engaging learning experiences, underpinned by our school values.
At our school, children feel safe to question and challenge themselves and others, are inspired to take risks and are equipped with the tools to succeed now and in later life.
Our children leave our school rich with knowledge, having found their passion and are well prepared for their next step and are sailing into their futures.
Our values underpin everything we do in school to provide our children with the firm foundations required both in school and life beyond.

Our Curriculum
Our curriculum is underpinned by our school values and provides purposeful and flexible learning experiences that develops children into responsible future citizens.
We provide knowledge rich learning which progressively builds on prior learning and connects knowledge, allowing children to stretch their minds.
We promote a positive climate where children feel safe to question and challenge themselves and others, empowering them to deepen their learning.
Our curriculum provides children with the tools to succeed now and in later life. Our aim is to nurture creativity and encourage problem solving and critical thinking.
Our children will leave our school with a wealth of knowledge and having found their passion for learning and are well prepared for their next step.
Please see our Whole School Curriculum by clicking here. Our most recent curriculum overviews are below:
Personal Development Learning Curriculum
At our school, we value Personal Development Learning (PDL). Our PDL curriculum encompasses Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE) as well as Relationships and Sex Education, Safeguarding, Mental Health and Wellbeing. Everything we do ties into our school values. Please find our policy and planning below:
Religious Education (RE)
Our school is based on an inclusive and broad minded ethos; we expect all children to attend collective Worship assemblies and participate in RE lessons. However, we respect the right of any parent/guardian to request permission for their child to be excused. Withdrawal will only be made following parental discussion with the Head teacher followed by written confirmation of withdrawal. The school will make alternative arrangements for the supervision of those children granted withdrawal from assemblies and lessons.
Music and Music Development Plan
At our school, music is taught regularly using a mixture of specialist music teachers and clear schemes of work. Click here for a copy of our music development plan.
